content.value_statement: Materials workflows often require complex structure, thermodynamic, and electronic analysis. This skill provides pymatgen guidance, reusable workflows, and focused scripts for common tasks.
actual_capabilities: Read, create, transform, and serialize crystal structures and molecules with pymatgen classes.
Convert individual or batched structure files across CIF, POSCAR, JSON, YAML, XYZ, and other supported formats.
Analyze composition, lattice properties, symmetry, coordination environments, and distance matrices.
Build Materials Project phase diagrams and assess stability, decomposition, and chemical potentials.
Guide electronic structure, surface, VASP input, diffraction, elasticity, and magnetic ordering workflows.
limitations: Python, pymatgen, and task-specific optional dependencies must be installed separately.
Materials Project queries require network access and a user-provided API key.
The bundled scripts do not execute external density functional theory calculations.
Results depend on input quality, scientific assumptions, and installed library versions.

use_cases.title: Compare Phase Stability
use_cases.description: Build a chemical-system phase diagram and review stable phases, decomposition products, and energy above hull.

use_cases.title: Normalize Structure Collections
use_cases.description: Convert mixed structure files into a consistent format and inspect symmetry, composition, and coordination.

use_cases.title: Prepare Simulation Inputs
use_cases.description: Generate organized VASP input sets for relaxation, static, and band-structure stages.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Crystal Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [structure file]. Report composition, lattice parameters, density, space group, and suspicious site geometry. Do not modify the source file.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Structure Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [input files] to [target format] in [output directory]. Preserve the originals and summarize successes, failures, and detected formulas.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Thermodynamic Stability
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [chemical system] phase diagram using Materials Project data. Analyze [composition] and explain stability, decomposition products, and relevant assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reproducible Screening Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a high-throughput workflow for [materials objective]. Include transformations, input generation, provenance, validation checks, failure handling, and output organization.

output_examples.input: Analyze a silicon CIF with symmetry and nearest-neighbor checks.
output_examples.output: A structured report covering formula, cell metrics, density, space group, equivalent sites, coordination counts, and geometry warnings.

output_examples.input: Convert a directory of POSCAR files to CIF while preserving originals.
output: A conversion summary with destination paths and detected formulas.
A clear list of files that failed parsing or conversion.
The original POSCAR files remain unchanged.

output_examples.input: Assess one composition within a ternary Materials Project phase diagram.
output_examples.output: A phase-stability summary describing hull position, likely decomposition products, stable competing phases, and data-source limitations.

best_practices: Keep source structures unchanged and write generated files to a dedicated output directory.
Validate symmetry, units, convergence, and physical assumptions before using results in research decisions.
Store API keys in environment variables and never place real credentials in prompts or shared files.
anti_patterns: Do not overwrite irreplaceable structure files during conversion or transformation.
Do not treat generated input sets as validated calculations without checking convergence settings.
Do not publish Materials Project results without recording query filters, versions, and retrieval context.

faq.question: Which structure formats are supported?
faq.answer: Pymatgen supports CIF, POSCAR, XYZ, JSON, YAML, and many formats from major computational chemistry codes.

faq.question: Is a Materials Project API key required?
faq.answer: Only Materials Project queries require a key. Local structure conversion and analysis do not require one.

faq.question: Does this skill run VASP or other simulation engines?
faq.answer: No. It can prepare inputs and analyze outputs, but external simulation software must run separately.

faq.question: Can the skill work offline?
faq.answer: Most local structure tasks work offline after dependencies are installed. Materials Project queries require network access.

faq.question: Will the bundled scripts modify input files?
faq.answer: The scripts read input structures and write separate outputs. Choose output paths carefully because existing destination files may be replaced.

faq.question: Which pymatgen versions are expected?
faq.answer: The documentation targets recent pymatgen releases, especially 2024.x and later. API behavior may differ across installed versions.
